subject.title: [Bug]: Terminal provider model_not_available in subagent announce path can trigger chat.history storm and gateway event-loop starvation

question: Should this composite report stay open as one cross-surface tracker, or should maintainers split it into canonical subagent-wake, provider-classification, config-validation, and gateway-availability work?
rationale: The source evidence shows real unresolved slices, but the safe permanent shape crosses product-sensitive boundaries: fail-closed model config validation, provider fallback semantics, subagent delivery durability, and gateway recovery behavior.

options.title: Keep Composite Tracker
options.body: Leave this issue open until the related subagent wake, provider wording, config validation, and gateway starvation proof are all covered or explicitly split.

options.title: Split To Canonicals
options.body: Move each remaining slice to the existing canonical issues and close this only after those links preserve the provider-error and event-loop evidence.

options.title: Sponsor One Cross-Surface Fix
options.body: Ask an owner to design and review one integrated change across provider classification, announce delivery, and gateway availability rather than queueing a normal automated fix.

recommendation.title: Keep Composite Tracker
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open until the related subagent wake, provider wording, config validation, and gateway starvation proof are all covered or explicitly split.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the broadest recent history across subagent lifecycle, provider/runtime refactors, and the product-sensitive boundaries involved here.
